To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the regional density of the VMAT2 in the human brain is quantifiable with [11C] DTBZ and PET, and that the VMAT2 density decreases with normal aging and is markedly decreased in Parkinson's disease.

the density of the type II vesicular monoamine transpoer (VMAT2), which transports the monoamine neurotransmitters into storage vesicles, is reduced in the putamen of Parkinson's disease patients compared with normal elderly controls, and that the rate of loss of VMAT2 in normal aging is about 0.77 percent per year.
VMAT2 density in the striatum is decreased by about 1% per year of normal aging and that the decrease is accelerated in Parkinson's disease.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of positron emission tomographic imaging of monoamine vesicular transporter (VMAT) binding sites to assess the integrity of the dopaminergic nigrostriatal system in Parkinson's disease.
the development of new radiopharmaceuticals for the imaging of the central nervous system by positron emission tomograph.

the development and application of a new positron emission tomographic (PET) radiopharmaceutical, [11C]Dihydrotetrabenzine ([11C]DTZ), which has potential as a marker of the integrity of nigrostriat dopaminergic neurons in patients with Parkinson's disease (pd) and other disorders involving the dopamine system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
VMAT2 is an excellent target for PET studies of the nigrostriatal dopaminergic system.
the present data are compatible with the hypothesis that the nigrostriatal system is involved in the pathophysiology of depression, but that this involvement is not specific to depression.
the VMAT2 binding in the striatum is reduced by 40–50% in PD, and by 20–30% in normal aging.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
[11C]Dihydrotetrabenzine PET is a promising tool for the objective quantification of the nigrostriatal dopaminergic system, including its evaluation in Parkinson's disease.
the VMAT2 PET ligand [11C]di-hydrotetrabenazone (DTBZ) is a useful probe of the integrity of the nigrostriatal dopamine system in Parkinson's disease.
the VMAT2 binding potential in the putamen of Parkinson's disease patients is reduced to 39% of normal and that the VMAT binding potential decreases with advancing age in the normal human brain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the VMAT2 ligand [11C]DHTBZ can be used as an in vivo biomarker of nigrostriata1 dopaminergic integrity.
the VMAT2 ligand [11C]Dihydrotetrabenzine (DTBZ) can be used in positron emission tomographic (PET) studies of Parkinson's disease (P.D.) to quantify nigrostriatal dopamine neuron integrity.
the [11C] DTBZ PET imaging technique can be used to measure VMAT2 density, which is a marker of dopamine neuron integrity in the brain.
